text:
Alex D: hey — followup from the pos-encoding regressions we saw on canary this morning. noticed fp16 runs blow up after ~8k seqs
Maria T: saw that too, logs show NaNs from the rope multiply path, accumulation gets huge
Jordan P: reproduced locally, pattern: long context + cached KV reuse + rotary scaled by diag terms. double-checking math looked fine though
Sasha K: my hunch: accumulation with fused attention kernel using fp16 reduce sums without guard leads to overflow on some kernels (tied to specific cuBLAS conv-alike kernels)
Eden (QA): test case attached to the failing harness: long_seq_rope_repro.py, we hit it in 3/10 runs on A100-80GB
Alex D: good — propose short-term defensive changes: 1) clamp accumulation (soft clamp eps) 2) add FP32 fallback path when detected during runtime 3) telemetry + metric for per-kernel saturation events
Maria T: +1. Implementation detail: we should not silently change outputs for all users. make clamp opt-in via runtime config and default to canary rollout
Jordan P: for the clamp, something like: 
```
float accum = sum(...);
if (!isfinite(accum) || fabs(accum) > CLAMP_THRESH) {
  accum = clamp(accum, -CLAMP_HI, CLAMP_HI);
}
```
Use a relative threshold (max_abs > 1e4 * expected) rather than absolute?
Sasha K: relative threshold sounds better. Also add small epsilon to denom on any divs and a tiny bias before softmax to avoid sticky extremes
Eden (QA): can we add deterministic test that asserts output L2 distance < 1e-3 compared to fp32 baseline for shorter seqs, and then detect divergence for long seqs? we need guard coverage
Alex D: yes. Tests: unit (small seq exact match), long-repro (regression harness), nightly stress (random long KVs). Add a test that runs with quantized kernels too
Maria T: another layer: kernel selector should tag kernels with a 'safety_profile' value: {fast, safe}. Selector policy: prefer fast; if telemetry reports saturation event, switch that model+kernel combo to 'safe' for that workload
Jordan P: that lets us keep perf for normal runs but automatically fall back for problematic ones. we'll need a cross-run tag stored in the model runtime metadata
Sasha K: PR idea: add an API in kernel_selector.cpp: bool kernel_reports_overflow(); and a per-request check to flip the runtime policy. simple TTL on the flip (eg 24h)
Alex D: exact. Also add a lightweight in-kernel counter (atomic) of saturation events aggregated and emitted every 5m by infra-bot
infra-bot: deploy: canary build finished: runtime:v2026.3-rope-safety deployed to canary cluster (3 hosts)
Eden (QA): I'll run the harness against that canary and post numbers in ~30m
Maria T: backlog items: 
- implement clamp + eps guards (PR)
- kernel selector flag + telemetry emission (PR)
- unit + long-run tests + CI job update
- docs: runtime config knobs (clamp thresholds, fallback enable)
Alex D: assign owners? Maria take kernel selector + telemetry, Jordan take clamp implementation in fused kernels, Sasha add epsilon guards + math asserts, Eden owns tests and regression harness automation
Maria T: ack, I'll open PR and include a toggle config: pos_enc_guard.enabled = true/false and pos_enc_guard.mode = "clamp|fp32_fallback|both"
Jordan P: starting clamp PR now, will reference harness: <https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/512> in description for context
Sasha K: I'll add small asserts in posenc impl: 
```
assert(isfinite(scale));
if (fabs(scale) > SCALE_WARN) log.warn("posenc scale suspicious", scale);
```
and fallthrough to safe path on assert failure in production builds (no crash)
Eden (QA): after PRs land, I'll run stress with 10k randomized seeds across 4 GPU types (A100, H100, 80GB variants) and report latencies + any correctness deltas
Alex D: long-term: consider rewriting posenc multiply as a numerically stable fuse that uses pairwise summation or Kahan-like accum, but that's a followup RFC. for now the defenses above should be enough to unblock Dedicated customer workloads
Maria T: timeline? aiming to get canary PRs in today, full rollout next week if no regressions
Jordan P: ping infra for canary scale if QA hits flakes
infra-bot: infra-note: canary pool capacity increased by 4 GPUs for test window 2h starting now
Alex D: perfect. action items posted to #eng-runtime-limbo board: https://phab.redwood.ai/T1234
Eden (QA): will post initial results in thread when done :hourglass_flowing_sand:
